title: Connect and Switchboard load processors and subgraphs from the HTTP registry at runtime, and Connect auto-installs the package for an unknown document type
content:
The Vetra package ecosystem shipped as one of v6.0.0's five highlights, and its behavioural claims are the ones that matter downstream:

- **Dynamic loading** — Connect and Switchboard load **processors and subgraphs at runtime** from the HTTP registry, with *no rebuild required* when a new package is published.
- **Auto-discovery** — Connect **automatically finds and installs the correct package when it encounters an unknown document type**. That is what makes the registry's `by-document-type` lookup a user-facing feature rather than an API curiosity.
- **Version picker** — the Connect UI lets a user choose a specific dist-tag version when installing.

The CLI surface is three commands against a private, npm-compatible, Verdaccio-backed registry:

```bash
ph publish                                  # publish a built package
ph install @your-org/your-package           # install (Powerhouse registry by default)
ph unpublish @your-org/your-package@1.0.0   # unpublish and purge the CDN cache
```

Two related v6 improvements that shape how those packages are built: **separate node and browser processor bundles** (processors publish distinct entrypoints), and tree-shaking work — `sideEffects: false` in generated boilerplate, with **pglite, jszip and renown crypto lazily loaded**. The last one is the same lazy-import discipline the knowledge-note package needs in production.

One breaking change from the same release still applies to any project carrying old output: **delete `src/subgraphs/`**, because subgraphs are now generated and loaded at runtime and a checked-in copy conflicts.
